docRequirement: plugins.md:209 lists `settings.json` at the plugin root as a first-class component location ("Default settings applied when the plugin is enabled"), and :298-308 binds the behaviour: "Plugins can include a `settings.json` file at the plugin root to apply default configuration when the plugin is enabled. Currently, only the `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` keys are supported." :300 — "Setting `agent` activates one of the plugin's custom agents as the main thread, applying its system prompt, tool restrictions, and model. This lets a plugin change how Claude Code behaves by default when enabled." :308 — "Settings from `settings.json` take priority over `settings` declared in `plugin.json`. Unknown keys are silently ignored." So four separable obligations: read the plugin-root file; honour `agent` as a main-thread override of prompt + tools + model; honour `subagentStatusLine`; and rank `settings.json` above the manifest's `settings` block while ignoring unknown keys.
current: The file is DETECTED and nothing else. `CLAUDE_RETAINED_SURFACE_FIELDS` carries one blanket row, `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:2275). `addClaudeRetainedSurfaceDeferrals` (:2278-2317, called at :270 with the bundle `rootDirectory`) fires on `existsSync(join(rootDirectory, 'settings.json'))` at :2297, pushes `{ externalKind: 'settings', reasonCode: 'plugin.deferred.claude_settings' }` (template at :2302), and stops. The file is never opened; neither key is ever parsed. `grep -ran "subagentStatusLine"` over packages/ apps/ scripts/ returns zero source hits, and the only reference to a plugin-root `settings.json` anywhere in packages/shared/src/plugins is that one line (`grep -ran 'settings\.json'` — every other hit is `.claude/settings.json` prose in mcpb-configuration.ts or the per-plugin MCPB option store at plugin-settings.ts:40, a different file with the same name). Three consequences follow from the detection-only row. (1) One row, not two: the `if (deferred.some(entry => entry.externalKind === externalKind)) continue;` dedupe at :2299 collapses `plugin.json`'s `settings` block and the root `settings.json` into a single record, so the documented priority order is not merely unimplemented, it is unrepresentable. (2) No author diagnostic: unlike the `themes` row (:2220-2253), this row carries no `refusal`, so the `diagnostics.push` at :2307-2314 never runs and the plugin author is told nothing at install. (3) The whole bundle is downgraded: `buildClaudeCompatibilityReport` sets `state: deferred.length > 0 ? 'partial' : 'supported'` (claude.ts:484), so shipping a `settings.json` makes an otherwise perfect bundle permanently `partial`. On first install that is invisible — `PluginManagementServiceV2.install` returns no `requiresConfirmation` (management-service-v2.ts:190-199), `describeInstallOutcome` therefore yields `blocked:false, needsConfirmEnable:false` (useMarketplaceInstall.ts:55-72), the guard at PluginsPage.tsx:291 skips recording the deferred list, and the user gets a plain success toast at :300. On any later update or repair it is not: `repairUnlocked` calls `this.policyStore.purgePlugin(...)` for a `partial` report (management-service-v2.ts:553-554) and returns `requiresConfirmation: true` (:572), `update()` is a pure alias of `repair()` (:579-581), and PluginsPage.tsx:424-432 flips the card to `needsConfirmEnable`, rendering the "Confirm enable" button at :1476-1481. The reason is never shown: the only renderer of `plugins.compatDeferredEntry` is `blockedInstallMessage` (PluginsPage.tsx:1851-1859), reachable only on a BLOCKED install. As for honouring `agent` by some other route, there is none: no main-thread-agent override exists anywhere in the fork. `StoredConfig` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:51-80) has `outputStyleId` and `defaultThinkingLevel` and no agent key at all; `loadAgentDefinitions`/`resolveAgentDefinition` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:652-731) only ever produce definitions for DELEGATED children; and the main-thread prompt built at packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6586-6608 takes no agent argument — the one place an agent definition's instructions are grafted onto a prompt is `this.config.childSystemPrompt` at :6615-6618, which is set for a spawned child only.
divergence: The whole mechanism is absent; only the file's existence is noticed. Nothing parses `settings.json`, so neither documented key is read, and no value is applied. Four deltas, separable: (a) `agent` — the fork has no main-thread-agent override to route it into, so this is not a wrong key name or a narrowed value, it is a missing capability class; the nearest existing seam is the child-only `childSystemPrompt` append at pi-agent.ts:6615 and the app-level `outputStyleId` knob at config/storage.ts:57, and neither has a main-thread agent analogue. (b) `subagentStatusLine` — zero source hits repo-wide; the whole statusline surface is separately absent and is owned by f206. (c) The priority rule (`settings.json` outranks `plugin.json`'s `settings`) is unrepresentable, not just unapplied: the externalKind dedupe at claude.ts:2299 emits one row for both spellings. (d) "Unknown keys are silently ignored" is trivially satisfied for the wrong reason — every key is ignored, known ones included. One thing that is NOT a delta and must not be re-fixed: the detection itself is correct and its `deferred` record is the right shape; what is missing beside it is the `refusal` diagnostic that the `themes` row at claude.ts:2247-2252 already demonstrates. And one behaviour we add that the doc does not ask for: a bundle whose only unsupported surface is a `settings.json` is marked `partial`, which costs it its activation grants on every update.

change.what: STEP 1, and it is the one-file fix worth landing on its own: replace the blanket `{ externalKind: 'settings', field: 'settings', defaultPath: 'settings.json' }` row with a real reader. Read `<root>/settings.json` as JSON, merge it OVER `input.settings` from the manifest (that is :308's priority rule — the merged object is what gets reported), keep only `agent` and `subagentStatusLine` and drop every other key without a word (:308 'Unknown keys are silently ignored'). Emit ONE deferred row PER unhonoured supported key that the bundle actually set — `plugin.deferred.claude_settings_agent` and `plugin.deferred.claude_settings_subagent_status_line` — instead of one row for the file's mere existence, and give each a `refusal` diagnostic in the shape of the `themes` row at :2247-2252, naming the key and saying the plugin's default will not be applied. Two consequences of doing it this way, both wanted: a `settings.json` that sets only unknown keys stops downgrading the bundle to `partial` at all (:484 counts rows, and there will be none), and an author who set `agent` finally hears about it at install. Do NOT drop the `settings` field spelling — a manifest `settings` block must go through the same merge.

The fixture is inventory-exact and asserts deferred rows in manifest field order (see the comment at claude.ts:266-269). Renaming one blanket row into per-key rows changes it. Update the fixture and the two suites that read it: packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/format-adapters.test.ts:1887-1890 and format-adapter-fixtures.test.ts:153, :310-313.

STEP 2 begins here, and only if the owner approves honouring `agent` at all (see notes). Carry the merged, key-filtered object into the IR as its own descriptor — `{ agent?: string }` — rather than reusing the existing `{ kind: 'setting'; valueType; defaultValue }` binding (resolver.ts:282), which is an MCPB user_config OPTION the user fills in, a different thing from a default the plugin asserts. Model the doc comment on PluginOutputStyleDescriptor at :515-534, which is the file's precedent for 'recorded, and here is exactly why it is or is not honoured'.

A bundle that stops being `partial` therefore stops losing its grants on update — an intended improvement, but it changes an observable the plugin-management tests assert. PERSISTENCE BOUNDARY (risk trigger): `compatibility` is stored with the installed plugin by `this.store.repair(...)` (management-service-v2.ts:555-566), so reason codes written by an older build stay on disk — the renderer must tolerate the retired `plugin.deferred.claude_settings` code, and the new config key at config/storage.ts must be optional so an older config.json still validates. WIRE BOUNDARY (risk trigger) for step 2 only: `SafeMarketplacePluginDeferredCapability` and the installed-plugin summary live in packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:438/:613-644; a new capability kind and any new Safe field cross the Electron IPC surface and are enumerated by the channel-map and ipc-channels parity tests. Step 2 also touches the highest-trust text in the turn — the main-thread system prompt at pi-agent.ts:6586 — and the agent-definition resolver whose reserved-name and builtin-collision rules (definitions.ts:666-669, :692-696) are the guard against a plugin impersonating `fork` or a built-in.
userImpact: Two things, one silent and one not. Silent: a user installs a Claude plugin whose whole point is to change the default behaviour — the doc's own example is a `security-reviewer` plugin — clicks Install on the Plugins page, gets a green 'installed' toast, and the agent never activates. Nothing in the app says so, and nothing says so to the plugin author either: the deferred row exists but the only code path that renders `plugins.compatDeferredEntry` is the blocked-install message at PluginsPage.tsx:1851-1859. Not silent, and arguably worse: because the file's mere presence forces `compatibility.state: 'partial'` (claude.ts:484), the FIRST time that user clicks Update or Repair on that plugin, `repairUnlocked` purges its activation grants (management-service-v2.ts:553-554), the plugin switches off, and the card shows a 'Confirm enable' shield button (PluginsPage.tsx:1476-1481) with no stated reason — the user sees a working plugin spontaneously disable itself after an update. That happens to any Claude bundle carrying a plugin-root `settings.json`, whatever it contains, including one whose keys we would ignore anyway.
